title: Monitoring of Huanglongbing (HLB) in Tahiti Lime (Citrus latifolia Tanaka) Plantations in the Department of Nariño, Colombia
content: Citrus cultivation in the department of Nariño represents a fundamental socioeconomic pillar for producers in the northern municipalities of this region; however, productivity is visually threatened by Huanglongbing (HLB), a disease caused by the bacterium "Candidatus Liberibacter asiaticus" (CLas) and transmitted by Diaphorina citri. This research monitored the epidemiological risk of HLB through symptoms associated with the disease, vector identification, its spatial distribution in Nariño, and the molecular detection of CLas in leaf tissue of Tahiti lime (Citrus latifolia Tanaka). Stratified and systematic sampling was conducted on farms in La Unión, San Lorenzo, Taminango, and El Rosario. Collected adults were identified using morphological characters; sites were georeferenced, and petioles and midveins were processed via CTAB DNA extraction and conventional PCR with primers OI1/OI2c targeting the 16S rRNA gene. The presence of D. citri was confirmed in all four municipalities, in all four municipalities, in plots under organic management and on trees with active flushing. Foliar symptoms compatible with HLB were observed; however, no field samples amplified for CLas—with the positive control yielding a 1,160 bp band—thus failing to molecularly confirm the presence of CLas.
